title: Semiprime algorithm proof explorer
intro: The mathematical factorization algorithm has a correctness proof. Its Boolean-stack implementation is being assembled from finalized components. The whole-program bit-complexity theorem remains open.
target_scope: For every semiprime N from its canonical binary input, ℓ = ⌈log₂(N+1)⌉, with fixed C and d chosen before N. This is a target, not an achieved running-time theorem.
pipeline_disclaimer: This is a curated algorithm reading order, not a Lean-extracted dependency graph. Adjacent stages do not assert that their physical caller joins are complete.
evidence_disclaimer: Finalized means recorded historical component gates, with their original scope. This explorer checks source and evidence hashes; it does not run Lean or promote drafts to verified results.

glossary.meaning: A theorem identifies the specified algorithm’s output. It does not by itself establish a primitive machine’s total running time.
A fixed physical program and its stated local contract passed the recorded focused gates. Read its input boundary: a prepared operand is not automatically acquired from N.
A physical program passes actually acquired words to the next program, paying for copies, parsing, cleanup, memory and returns.
One deterministic original-input program factors every semiprime within the displayed bound, including preprocessing, recursive coefficients, storage and factor recovery.
